what: A SIGTERM inside a few syscalls of a tool's own lifetime left what the stop was meant to remove. SharedCodeAudit465Tests.test_a_child_past_its_ceiling_is_stopped_and_cleans_up failed once on macOS CI with .verify_big_x.mp4.ffskill-lock in verify.py's --out: the export step got its SIGTERM from verify.py's 1 s limit while export.py was in _OutputLock.__enter__, after os.link made the lock and before __enter__ returned. The handler's SystemExit came out of __enter__, so the with block was never entered and its __exit__ never ran. On a slow runner the 1 s limit lands at the lock (export.py makes it about 0.35-0.5 s after start on Linux), elsewhere mid-encode, where the with block removes it. The same window inside __exit__ (after it dropped its descriptor, before the removal), and between a child's Popen and _watch() in run()'s two runners, run_tool(), verify.py's step and batch.py's main-thread step: stop_children() did not know the child, which ran on and wrote its output (and, a sibling script, its lock) after the parent had said its partial output was removed; on macOS ffmpeg has no PR_SET_PDEATHSIG and finished the file.
escaped: The A183 test stops a step at whatever point 1 s reaches, which on Linux and Windows and on most macOS runs is the encode, inside the with block. #510 handled a second signal raised inside the lock's __exit__, not a first one; nothing stopped a tool at the lock's creation or at a child's start.
mechanism: runner._signals_held(): in the main thread a SIGINT/SIGTERM that arrives in the block is handled when it ends (runner._on_signal and batch.py's _interrupt record it as pending). The lock's creation and removal and every Popen-then-_watch run in one, and _on_signal removes every lock this process holds (runner._LOCKS, registered in __enter__) itself instead of relying on the unwinding. test_contract.SharedCodeAudit465Tests.test_a_stop_inside_a_lock_s_making_or_a_child_s_start_leaves_nothing sends the tool SIGTERM in each window (after the lock's link, inside its removal, after ffmpeg's start under run(), after a sibling's start under run_tool(), after a batch step's start) and asserts no lock, no partial output and no step left running.
